findings.evidence: No evals/ directory: no evals/evals.json and no evals/trigger-queries.json. The skill ships no tracked .py/.sh script (only codemod_template.py.txt), so D7 uses the 8/7 split; tests/test_gate_scope.py, tests/test_setup.py and tests/test_wizard_app_1.py only assert catalog title and the template path and are not scored.
findings.fix: Add evals/evals.json with at least three realistic prompts (casual and precise, plus a name-collision edge case), expected output, input files under evals/files/, and verifiable assertions; add evals/trigger-queries.json with about 20 queries, 8-10 should-trigger and 8-10 should-not-trigger including near-misses such as a single-file Edit or a sed-safe unique rename.

findings.evidence: LibCST parses source into a Concrete Syntax Tree, matches syntax nodes (not raw text), transforms them, and serializes back — comments, whitespace, and style preserved.
findings.fix: Delete the Overview definition of a concrete syntax tree; keep the decision table, the name-only matching landmine, and the subcommand examples.

findings.evidence: Choose codemod vs alternatives is a decision table, but the body never states the thinking check before a run (is this identifier unique, or does another library also define it?) and Notes restates validation and uv without a procedure.
findings.fix: Before the table, add: before choosing a tool, ask whether the identifier is unique in the repo and whether any imported library defines the same name; if either is no, narrow --paths and audit the diff, or write a QualifiedNameProvider codemod. Drop the Notes lines that only repeat 'run tests' and 'prefer uv run'.

findings.evidence: Do not alter string literals or comments unless explicitly required.
findings.fix: Delete the Notes restatement. The NEVER list already says not to touch string literals or comments, and the name-only matching bullet already gives the hard-won reason.

findings.evidence: Use when refactoring Python with LibCST codemods — multi-file renames of classes, methods, constants, or function parameters where comments and formatting must survive and naive sed/search-replace would also hit strings and comments (codemods match by name, not by scope or type). Includes a bundled codemod_template.py.txt (copy into the project as tools/codemod_template.py) with subcommands rename-symbol, rename-parameter, add-parameter, remove-parameter, rewrite-docstring.
findings.fix: Refactor Python with LibCST codemods so comments and formatting survive: multi-file renames of classes, methods, constants, or parameters, signature changes, and scoped docstring rewrites. Use when a rename or signature change spans files and sed or search-replace would also hit strings, comments, or longer identifiers, even if the user never says LibCST or codemod. Keywords: LibCST, codemod, rename-symbol, rename-parameter, add-parameter, remove-parameter, rewrite-docstring, CST. Not for a single-line or single-file edit, a unique name that sed can rename safely, or non-Python files.

Name the skill directory explicitly and gate the copy: copy skills/cst-refactor/codemod_template.py.txt to tools/codemod_template.py only when tools/codemod_template.py does not already exist; do not load the template into context when the project already has it.

findings.evidence: Tighten matchers or use LibCST metadata when you need to avoid false positives.
findings.fix: Replace that sentence with the default already implied by the NEVER list: keep --paths narrow and read the whole diff; write a custom QualifiedNameProvider codemod only when the diff still renames a symbol the project does not own. Do not leave 'tighten matchers' as an equal option.

findings.evidence: uv run python tools/codemod_template.py add-parameter --function run_migration --param debug --default False --paths src --include-tests
findings.fix: State the outcomes the template actually produces and the cases it skips: add-parameter without a default appends a required parameter and, without --call-value, does not update call sites; add and remove never touch *args or **kwargs; rewrite-docstring only replaces text inside the first simple-string statement of a class or function body and skips f-strings, concatenated strings, and module docstrings; a missing path raises ValueError before any file is written, and a parse error stops mid-run with earlier files already saved. Add one example of the narrow-path-then-audit branch for a shared name such as connect.
